questions.question: How do you test models and controllers in Rails?
questions.title: Testing Models and Controllers
questions.direct_answer: Model tests check rules in isolation: assert a validation (assert_not Post.new(title: '').save), a scope (assert_equal [p1,p2], Post.published), a method (assert_equal 80, post.excerpt.length). Controller tests (or request tests) check the HTTP layer: get '/posts/42'; assert_response :success; assert_equal 'My Post', response.body. In Rails 7, request tests (integration-style) are preferred over old controller tests — they hit the route, run the full stack, and check the response. Fixtures (test/fixtures/posts.yml) or factories seed test data. Run a single file with rails test test/models/post_test.rb; the whole suite with rails test.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know model tests check validations/scopes/methods and request tests check the HTTP layer (get, assert_response, response.body).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Testing the framework (that .save works) instead of YOUR logic, or coupling tests to internals.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Model tests: validations/scopes/methods in isolation. Request tests: get '/x'; assert_response; response.body. Fixtures/factories seed data; rails test runs them.

sections.title: Isolate Rules, Then Hit the HTTP Layer
sections.content: Model tests check rules in isolation: assert a validation (assert_not Post dot new title empty save), a scope (assert_equal p1 p2, Post dot published), a method (assert_equal 80, post dot excerpt dot length). Controller or request tests check the HTTP layer: get slash posts 42; assert_response success; assert_equal My Post, response dot body. In Rails 7, request tests (integration-style) are preferred over old controller tests — they hit the route, run the full stack, and check the response. Fixtures (test slash fixtures slash posts dot yml) or factories seed test data. Run a single file with rails test test slash models slash post_test dot rb; the whole suite with rails test.

sections.title: Model vs Request Tests
sections.content:
Model: rules in isolation. Request: get -> assert_response -> response.body. Fixtures/factories seed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[model test: validation/scope/method] --> R[request test: get /posts/42]
  R --> A[assert_response :success]
  A --> B[assert_equal ..., response.body]
```

sections.title: Model and controller tests
sections.content:
```ruby
# test/models/post_test.rb (MODEL: rules in isolation)
class PostTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test 'title is required' do
    p = Post.new(title: '')
    assert_not p.valid?               # validation
    assert p.errors[:title].any?
  end

  test 'published scope' do
    p1 = Post.create!(title: 'a', published_at: Time.current)
    p2 = Post.create!(title: 'b', published_at: nil)
    assert_includes Post.published, p1
    assert_not_includes Post.published, p2
  end
end

# test/controllers/posts_controller_test.rb (REQUEST: HTTP layer)
class PostsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test 'GET show returns the post' do
    post = Post.create!(title: 'My Post', body: 'x')
    get post_path(post)                  # hit the route (full stack)
    assert_response :success             # 200
    assert_includes response.body, 'My Post'
  end

  test 'POST create makes a post' do
    assert_difference('Post.count', 1) do
      post posts_path, params: { post: { title: 'New', body: 'y' } }
    end
    assert_response :redirect
  end
end
# Run one file:  rails test test/models/post_test.rb
# Run all:       rails test
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Testing the framework (that .save works) instead of YOUR logic.
Coupling tests to internals (test behavior, not implementation).
Using old controller tests in Rails 7 (request tests are preferred).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Model tests check rules in isolation: validations, scopes, methods.
Request tests check the HTTP layer: get '/x', assert_response, response.body.
Rails 7 prefers request tests (integration-style) over old controller tests.
Fixtures (test/fixtures/*.yml) or factories seed test data.
Run one file (rails test test/models/post_test.rb) or all (rails test).

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Model tests check rules in isolation: assert a validation (assert_not Post dot new title empty save), a scope (assert_equal p1 p2, Post dot published), a method (assert_equal 80, post dot excerpt dot length). Controller or request tests check the HTTP layer: get slash posts 42; assert_response success; assert_equal My Post, response dot body. In Rails 7, request tests (integration-style) are preferred over old controller tests — they hit the route, run the full stack, and check the response. Fixtures (test slash fixtures slash posts dot yml) or factories seed test data. Run a single file with rails test test slash models slash post_test dot rb; the whole suite with rails test. A common mistake is testing the framework, like that save works, instead of your logic, and coupling tests to internals, when you should test behavior.
